top_five.text: The Ebola outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused over 4,200 deaths among 8,728 confirmed cases, with cross-border transmission now confirmed in Kenya.
A Russian strike on two buses killed at least 30 civilians in Ukraine as escalating shelling and drone strikes force widespread evacuations in eastern cities.
Yemen's Houthis claimed a missile attack on Riyadh airport that killed three Saudi citizens and wounded several others, marking a severe cross-border escalation.
Gang violence in Haiti has caused more than 5,000 deaths and injuries, worsening protection concerns and humanitarian distress across affected communities.
UN Women reports nearly 50,000 women and girls in Gaza have been killed or severely injured over three years of conflict, where military strikes persist despite ceasefire efforts.

The attack late on Thursday was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia since the kingdom and allied forces in neighbouring Yemen launched a major military offensive last weekend against the Iran-backed Houthis. Middle East.body: Nearly 50,000 women and girls in Gaza have been killed or severely injured since October 2023, according to UN Women. The agency says this amounts to one in 21 Gazan women and girls losing their life or living with lifelong disabilities. Nearly one million women and girls have been forced from their homes after more than 150 evacuation and movement orders. UN Women says women-led organisations are struggling to meet rising needs amid food insecurity, displacement and limited access to aid. Africa.headline: DRC/Kenya — Ebola outbreak deaths pass 4,200 as virus spreads to Kenya
Africa.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused 4,205 confirmed deaths among 8,728 confirmed cases recorded since May, according to reports citing the World Health Organization. The outbreak carries a case fatality rate of approximately 48.2 percent, with 775 new confirmed cases and 379 fatal cases registered between late September and early October. Cross-border transmission risks materialized as Kenya confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease following the death of a patient in a Nairobi hospital. Regional authorities continue contact tracing operations reaching nearly five million people to contain further transmission.
verified_figures: 775 new cases recorded between late September and early October

Africa.headline: Uganda — Clinical trials begin for candidate Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine
Africa.body: Phase Ib clinical trials for a new candidate vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain began in Uganda on October 6, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention announced. The ChAdOx1 vaccine, developed by the University of Oxford, is being evaluated to strengthen prevention measures as the disease spreads in the region. Concurrently, clinical trials for Ebola therapeutics are advancing, with more than 600 patients enrolled to evaluate medical treatments alongside ongoing contact tracing and surveillance efforts.
verified_figures: More than 600 participants enrolled in therapeutics clinical trials

Europe.headline: Residents of Ukraine's Kramatorsk forced to flee as drone strikes intensify
Europe.body: The city of Kramatorsk, in eastern Ukraine, is increasingly coming under Russian attack. For those who have stayed behind, the threat from drones and shelling has become a daily reality. Many have resisted leaving their homes, despite the growing danger – but now, more and more residents are being forced to flee. Our colleagues at France 2 followed an evacuation from the city and witnessed first-hand the dangers that residents face.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Afghanistan — Humanitarian Crisis Deepens Amid Returns and Aid Cuts
Asia-Pacific.body: A United Nations Development Programme report indicates that an estimated 28 million people in Afghanistan lived in poverty in 2025 as the country experienced deepening economic and humanitarian challenges. The crisis has been intensified by reduced international aid, prolonged drought, and the return of approximately 2.9 million Afghans over the course of the year. These population returns pushed an additional 1.4 million people into economic hardship. Despite recording a second consecutive year of real gross domestic product growth, Afghanistan continues to face widespread deprivation driven by environmental shocks and declining external support.
verified_figures: 1.4 million additional people pushed into hardship

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Floods and landslides in Chile: More than 1.000 people evacuated, six injured
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Heavy rains caused flooding and landslides in and around Chile's capital Santiago, causing more than 1.000 people to be evacuated and at least six people injured. President Chile Jose Antonio Cast declared a state of emergency in Las Condes, an eastern suburb of the capital, after flash floods blocked major roads, Insider reports. The area has received 144 millimeters of rain in recent days, which is about nine times more than the average rainfall for October, said Santiago Mayor Catalina San Martín.
